anti_tick_rules_written_before_any_prose: THE KEEP STAYS SHALLOW. THE GROUND UNDER EVERY ONE OF THESE THINGS HAS ALREADY MOVED AND IS NOT GOING TO STOP. NOTHING IS LIFTED AND NOTHING UNDER ANYTHING IS OPENED. WORK GOES IN FROM THE SIDE OR FROM THE FRONT AND THE THING ITSELF STAYS WHERE IT IS.

NO CHAPTER ENDS ON A JOB FINISHED. FOUR END ON A THING LEFT AS IT IS AND NOT PUT THERE BY THIS WORK: 0845 THE GREEN SEAM OF MOSS IN THE JOINT UNDER THE HOUSE WALL, 0847 THE BAND OF PALER PLASTER BEHIND THE STORE RAIL, 0849 THE CHIP OUT OF THE ARRIS ON THE THIRD SLAB, 0853 THE ONE JOINT THAT WAS NOT FED UNDER THE LIPPED FLAG BY THE RAIL. THE OTHER SIX END ON WHAT THE WORK SHOWED OR REVEALED.

THE SECOND PERSON IS SHOWN AND NEVER REPORTED. NOBODY IS TOLD, NOBODY IS REFUSED, NOBODY IS PASSED ANYTHING, NOTHING PASSES BETWEEN PEOPLE ABOUT THE JOB, NOBODY HOLDS ANYTHING OF OURS AND NOBODY LOOKS TWICE.
A FIGURE THE CHAPTER ITSELF SETS MUST CLOSE. WHERE A COUNT IS MADE IT IS MADE ONCE AND THE ENDING KEEPS IT. SINGLE-PLACE COUNTS ONLY.

THE THREE BLINDING JOBS ARE THREE DIFFERENT MATERIALS FOR THREE DIFFERENT REASONS AND MUST NOT READ AS ONE JOB THREE TIMES: 0845 IS FINE DUST ON A LEVEL RUN, 0849 IS A SWEEPING BLINDING ON A RUN THAT TAKES WASHING, 0853 IS GRIT ON A FALL BECAUSE DUST ON A FALL WASHES OUT AGAIN. THE WORD BLINDED MAY NOT BE THE SUBJECT OF TWO OF THEM.

bands.rotation_in_chapter_order: TWELVE, NINE, UNIT, LOCK-UP, TEN, TEN, LOCK-UP, UNIT, NINE, TWELVE. THE SECOND HALF IS THE MIRROR OF THE FIRST AND NOT A REPEAT OF IT. A WRITER OF 0855 ONWARD MAY NOT TAKE THIS ORDER WITHOUT SAYING SO.
bands.the_band_belongs_to_the_person: The seventy-eight woman is number twelve and has her sister. The woman in her late fifties is number nine and is alone in the house. bands.one_figure_per_chapter: One band figure in each chapter and only that one. No second pair of hands anywhere in the ten.

family: FAMILY IS ONE SOUND SHALLOW KEEP ON GROUND THAT HAS ALREADY MOVED. Nothing lifted, nothing opened, and every job is packing, brushing, sweeping, raking or easing into the outside of something that is already there. No customer told, refused, passed or finished inside the day. The second person is never reported: she or he comes, does a thing of his or her own, and goes. Why not nearest: 825-834 was work done properly on a thing going to be taken away; 815-824 was nobody asked and nobody measuring. Here nothing is going anywhere and the ground itself is the only thing that has moved, and the whole of it is keeping what is already sound from going unsound.
figure_rule_for_this_block: Five standing figures, one band each, kept for the whole block, and no figure anywhere in the ten is aged except those five. The late fifties stays at number nine alone, two chapters, 0846 and 0853. Roster by eyes: 0845 seventy-eight, 0846 late fifties, 0847 early forties, 0848 late forties, 0849 early thirties, 0850 early thirties, 0851 late forties, 0852 early forties, 0853 late fifties, 0854 seventy-eight. THE NEW UNAGED CEILING FOR THIS BLOCK IS FOUR AND THIS BLOCK USES ZERO.
declared_ordinary_word_note: Declared before any prose of 845 to 854 exists. It may not be not, usually, anyway, like, just, enough, still, kind, quite, small, round, one, week, almost, anything, and then, nearly, away, count, garden, shoulder, work, or any other word this file declares. EDGE is the ordinary word of this block, because nine of the ten jobs are on the edge of something: a gate joint, a kerb face, a rail edge, a guide, a slab face, a mouth, a bracket, a drawer front, a flag joint and a sash channel. Its figure is reported after the prose and not before.

cards.0845: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has the dust gone out of the joints of the run between the gate and the step, and means to brush every joint out and lay fine dust back into it without lifting a flag; the stop is where the dust stays in the joint below the level of the flags.
cards.0846: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has grass grown over the kerb and down the gutter along the front, and means to cut it back off the kerb face without moving the kerb; the stop is where the gutter line is open and falling to the gully.
cards.0847: At the unit a man in his early forties has the brush strip in the store rail packed with dust and grit over the summer, and means to comb it clean in place without lifting it out; the stop is where the bristles stand up and spring back along the whole length.
cards.0848: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has dust and ground grit packed into the two guides the roller shutter runs in, and means to brush both channels down without taking the shutter out of them; the stop is where the curtain comes down without the bang at the bottom.
cards.0849: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a run of four slabs with the soil film on the faces and the sand gone out of the joints, and means to sweep the faces and lay the sweepings back into the joints without lifting a slab; the stop is where a heel across a joint leaves no print.
cards.0850: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a sack of topsoil standing in the shed that has settled into a cone with a hollow down the middle, and means to turn the bottom of it over inside the sack without emptying it; the stop is where the soil runs loose to the hand at the mouth.
cards.0851: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has a cable tray dusted and packed with the grit off the yard against the conduit in it, and means to dust the tray and check the washer under every bracket head without moving the conduit; the stop is where the conduit lies clear the length of the bay with nothing resting on it.
cards.0852: At the unit a man in his early forties has the front of the bench drawer sticking on the swollen runner and rubbed a bright patch on its corner, and means to ease it with wax worked into the bearing edge without opening the drawer; the stop is where the front closes on its own without being pushed.
cards.0853: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has the joints of the path opened out where the run falls, and means to brush them out and pack them with grit without lifting a flag; the stop is where nine joints take grit to the level of the flags and the tenth cannot be fed from the top.
cards.0854: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has the sash channels packed with the dust and grit of the summer, and means to raise the lower sash and brush them out from outside without removing the sash; the stop is where the sash comes back down over the channels without catching.

second_measure_done_before_any_prose.method: The ten closings under closing_images were read side by side and three words were written against each one naming what that closing is actually about. figure_rule_for_the_block_on_arithmetic: NO FIGURE-MISMATCH SPREAD, NO TELEPHONE, NO SUM WORKED OUT TO REVEAL SOMETHING, AND NO NUMBER ASKED TO AGREE WITH A NUMBER IN ANOTHER CHAPTER. Counting physical things in one place and letting that count carry the chapter is the trade, and single-place counts are what this block uses. No arithmetic engine.
still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets on bearers. A shutter that runs silent. A near gate square with a brace in it. A gate on a wall that shuts. A back door shut on its own frame. A cowl braced on a plate. Grass on ground that has not had anything on it. A shelf under a window with a tub on it. Four feet of frost wall with its top course open. A spanner on a set of flags. Six feet of edging in a heap with the blue string on it. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out nine blocks and would be a tenth in this one: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame that is out of square; a landing wall with a bare patch; a fourth room at the top of a stair. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.

prohibitions_honoured.everything_dry_and_from_the_ground: Every job is dry and from the outside of the thing. No roof, no ladder, no loft, no manhole. No tap run and no water drawn, carried, poured or emptied by the person at work in any of the ten. The only water anywhere is the shopping woman's own bags at nine and nothing that is poured.
prohibitions_honoured.standing_objects_untouched: The freeholder does not arrive. The line at ten is not put right. The ladder at twelve is not opened and is not used in 0854, where the sash is raised on its own nails and held with the blue string off the edging heap. The box, its drawers and its lid are not opened. The coal at nine stays shut. No front room is entered in any of the ten. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring on the tiles. Ply neither touched nor nailed. The staple is NOT DONE and April is NOT PAGE and the latch stays hooked. Frost NOT TOUCHED. Spanner NOT PICKED. Oval holes NOT FILLED PLUGGED. No cement, no mortar, no new concrete.
prohibitions_honoured.no_arithmetic_engine: No figure-mismatch spread, no telephone, no sum, and no number asked to agree with another. Single-place counts only and every figure set closes.
